clue.text: Posthumous marriage said to make difficulties for her

definitions.text: Posthumous marriage said to make difficulties for her

parts.words: Posthumous marriage said to make difficulties for her
parts.note: Posthumus Leonatus in Shakespeare's Cymbeline is secretly married, and the slanders told of his wife cause her great trouble; 'Posthumous' looks like 'after death'

explanation.walkthrough: In Cymbeline the hero is Posthumus; his wife is slandered by Iachimo, whose lies bring her endless trouble.
explanation.definitionFit: The heroine of Cymbeline is the wife whose marriage to Posthumus brings her suffering.

clue.text: Encountered religious education in poetic measure

parts.note: encountered means met
RE is the abbreviation for religious education, a British school subject

explanation.surface: Someone met religious instruction in the form of verse rhythm.
explanation.definitionFit: Metre is the regular rhythm or measure of verse.

clue.text: Italian prizefighter celebrated by Bird

parts.note: Robert Montgomery Bird wrote a famous American play about Spartacus, a fighter in the Roman arena; 'Bird' looks like an animal

explanation.walkthrough: Bird is the American dramatist Robert Montgomery Bird, whose 1831 play about Spartacus was a huge stage success.
explanation.definitionFit: A Roman arena combatant fought for the prize of survival, and Bird's play took that title.

clue.text: Some fabulous swimmers

parts.note: fabulous here means belonging to fable or myth, so these are mythical water creatures

explanation.definitionFit: Water nymphs of Greek myth lived in rivers and springs, so they are legendary swimmers.

clue.text: There, mid revisions of Victorian poet

indicators.note: revisions rework a text, so the letters of the preceding words are rearranged

explanation.surface: Somewhere in the middle of redrafting, a Victorian poet's work is revised.
explanation.definitionFit: George Meredith was a novelist and poet of the Victorian era, author of Modern Love.

clue.text: Theroux offered it -some private knowledge of mine? The other fellow's Conservative

parts.note: something privately known to me is my secret
belonging to another man is his
a Tory is a member of the UK Conservative Party

explanation.surface: A writer hands over a confession, though the other man turns out to be a Conservative.
explanation.definitionFit: Paul Theroux published a novel of this title in 1989, so it is a book he offered readers.

clue.text: His Garden of Florence (perhaps exceptionally?) not a portrait

definitions.text: His Garden of Florence (perhaps exceptionally?) not a portrait

parts.words: His Garden of Florence (perhaps exceptionally?) not a portrait
parts.note: His namesake Sir Joshua was famed for portraits, so this work by a man of that surname was not one

explanation.walkthrough: Two men share the surname: Sir Joshua the portrait painter and John Hamilton the poet who wrote The Garden of Florence.
explanation.definitionFit: The poet John Hamilton Reynolds wrote The Garden of Florence, unlike the portraitist Sir Joshua.

clue.text: Old city in sad comeback for French writer

indicators.note: in places the ancient city inside the other piece
a comeback is a return, so the word sad is read backwards

parts.note: the word sad as written
Ur is the ancient city of Mesopotamia

explanation.surface: An ancient city stages a melancholy return for a French author.
explanation.walkthrough: 'comeback' reads the word backwards and 'in' sets the ancient Mesopotamian city inside; 'sad' looks like part of the picture but is the fodder.
explanation.definitionFit: Marguerite Duras was a French novelist and screenwriter, author of The Lover.

clue.text: Variety of pear favoured by Theophilus Grantly?

definitions.text: Variety of pear favoured by Theophilus Grantly?

parts.words: Variety of pear favoured by Theophilus Grantly?
parts.note: a warden is an old English cooking pear; Archdeacon Theophilus Grantly appears in Trollope's novel about Septimus Harding, the hospital's keeper

explanation.walkthrough: Archdeacon Grantly is a leading character in Trollope's first Barsetshire novel, and a warden is also an old variety of baking pear.
explanation.definitionFit: Trollope's novel shares its title with an old English baking pear, and Grantly is one of its characters.

clue.text: Russian player who scored several times for Diaghilev

definitions.text: Russian player who scored several times for Diaghilev

parts.words: Russian player who scored several times for Diaghilev
parts.note: scored means wrote music, as the composer did for Diaghilev's Ballets Russes; 'player' and 'scored' suggest a footballer

explanation.walkthrough: Firebird, Petrushka and The Rite of Spring were all composed for Diaghilev's company.
explanation.definitionFit: Igor Stravinsky was the Russian composer who wrote several ballet scores for Diaghilev.

clue.text: Concerning journalist poet

parts.note: re means concerning or about
ED is short for editor, a journalist

explanation.surface: A piece about a reporter who also writes verse.
explanation.definitionFit: Henry Reed was an English poet, author of Naming of Parts.

clue.text: Merry friend of Bilbo

parts.note: Merry is not cheerful here but the nickname of a hobbit in Tolkien

explanation.definitionFit: Meriadoc Brandybuck, called Merry, is a young hobbit relative and friend of Bilbo Baggins.

clue.text: Bard of strategic services with Scottish name

parts.note: OSS is the Office of Strategic Services, the wartime US intelligence agency
Ian is a typically Scottish first name

explanation.surface: A wartime intelligence man with a Scottish name turns out to be a poet.
explanation.definitionFit: Ossian was the legendary Gaelic bard whose supposed poems Macpherson published.

clue.text: Inconsequential dialogue is part of French attitude

indicators.note: part of says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Idle talk is just part of the French way of looking at things.
explanation.definitionFit: Light informal talk of no great importance is small talk.

clue.text: Wounding fact revealed in The Kingfisher?

definitions.text: Wounding fact revealed in The Kingfisher?

parts.words: Wounding fact revealed in The Kingfisher?
parts.note: The Kingfisher is a play by William Douglas Home, so a fact revealed in it is one of his truths; a painful candid fact goes by the same phrase

explanation.walkthrough: The Kingfisher (1977) is a comedy by the playwright William Douglas Home.
explanation.definitionFit: An unwelcome but accurate fact about oneself is the phrase; Home's play could show a truth of his.

clue.text: "Where can it be / This land of . . ?". asked Poe

definitions.text: "Where can it be / This land of . . ?". asked Poe

parts.words: "Where can it be / This land of . . ?". asked Poe
parts.note: a quotation to complete from Poe's poem about a knight's search for a fabled golden land

explanation.definitionFit: The legendary city of gold sought by explorers gives Poe's poem its title and refrain.

clue.text: The wild winds sung the dirge of this Scott creation

definitions.text: The wild winds sung the dirge of this Scott creation

parts.words: The wild winds sung the dirge of this Scott creation
parts.note: a line from Harold's ballad in Scott's Lay of the Last Minstrel about a drowned lady of the St Clairs

explanation.definitionFit: The lovely lady of Harold's ballad in Scott's poem drowns, and the winds lament her.

clue.text: Brother artist

parts.note: brother here means a friar, a religious brother, who was also a painter

explanation.definitionFit: Fra Angelico was a Dominican friar and early Renaissance painter, so a religious brother.

clue.text: "There are no fields of — on this side of the grave" (W. S. Landor, Imaginary Conversations)

definitions.text: "There are no fields of — on this side of the grave" (W. S. Landor, Imaginary Conversations)

parts.words: "There are no fields of — on this side of the grave" (W. S. Landor, Imaginary Conversations)
parts.note: a quotation to complete from Landor, the missing word being the legendary unfading flower

explanation.definitionFit: The imaginary flower that never fades stands for immortality, fitting fields beyond the grave.

clue.text: Courage of La Baronne Dudevant

definitions.meaning: grit or nerve, as in American slang 'to have ...'
Aurore Dupin, Baronne Dudevant, wrote under a male pen name

explanation.surface: A tribute to the bravery of a French baroness.
explanation.definitionFit: George Sand was the pen name of Baronne Dudevant, and grit is a colloquial word for courage.

clue.text: Poet may come to such conclusions

definitions.text: Poet may come to such conclusions

parts.words: Poet may come to such conclusions
parts.note: conclusions here are the short closing stanzas of a poem, not judgements reached

explanation.definitionFit: Short final stanzas ending a ballade are closing sections a poet may write.

clue.text: Essayist belonging to a chaste electorate

indicators.note: belonging to says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: An essay writer is a member of a virtuous body of voters.
explanation.definitionFit: Richard Steele founded The Tatler and wrote essays for The Spectator with Addison.

clue.text: European ruler managing with difficulty

parts.note: a king is a ruler

explanation.surface: A European monarch is struggling to get by.
explanation.definitionFit: Making a living or supply last by careful economy is to scrape by, with difficulty.

clue.text: 19 with small town American poet

parts.note: the answer to 19 across, a word for courage
a burg is an American word for a small town

explanation.surface: A small town with grit has produced a poet from the States.
explanation.definitionFit: Carl Sandburg was an American poet, author of Chicago Poems.

clue.text: Point in trick ballet

indicators.note: in places the compass point inside the word for a trick

parts.note: a ruse is a trick
S, south, is a point of the compass

explanation.surface: A piece of deception lies at the heart of a ballet.
explanation.walkthrough: The word is Russian in French, as in Diaghilev's Ballets Russes.
explanation.definitionFit: Ballet russe is the Russian-style ballet of Diaghilev's company, the word naming that kind of dance.

clue.text: I put back South American lingua franca

indicators.note: back says the letters of I put are read in reverse order

explanation.surface: Someone returns a common South American tongue to its place.
explanation.definitionFit: Tupi was a Brazilian native language used widely as a common trade tongue.

clue.text: Strangely cool antics of heretic

indicators.note: strangely says the letters of the following words appear in an unusual arrangement

explanation.surface: Odd cool behaviour is typical of a dissenter.
explanation.definitionFit: One who attacks cherished beliefs, originally images in church, is a dissenter from orthodoxy.

clue.text: Wouk treatment of Greene theme lacking power?

definitions.text: Wouk treatment of Greene theme lacking power?

parts.words: Wouk treatment of Greene theme lacking power?
parts.note: Take away the power and what remains is the title of a Herman Wouk novel

explanation.walkthrough: Strip 'The Power and' from Greene's title and Herman Wouk's 1994 novel of Israel is what is left.
explanation.definitionFit: Herman Wouk's novel of Israel's history is the end of Greene's title without its first part.

clue.text: Provenance of nineteenth-century nightingale

parts.note: the nightingale is the soprano Jenny Lind, a celebrated singer, not a bird

explanation.walkthrough: Jenny Lind, the soprano, was nicknamed the Swedish Nightingale.
explanation.definitionFit: Jenny Lind came from Stockholm, so her provenance is that Scandinavian country.
